title: Bile Diversion Procedure in Mice
author: Vance L. Albaugh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zdcf22w

steps.title: Preoperative Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the mice for surgery through housing and medication.

substeps.instruction: Singly-house all animals.
Administer preoperative pain medications: Ketoprofen (5 mg/kg) and Buprenorphine (0.05 mg/kg).
Ensure adequacy of anesthesia.
Immobilize the mouse gently on a surgical board/field.
Prep and drape the animal sterilely.

steps.title: Abdominal Access
steps.instruction: Perform a midline laparotomy to expose the surgical site.

substeps.instruction: Make a midline laparotomy incision with sharp surgical scissors, staying on the linea alba and away from the rectus abdominus muscles.

steps.title: Bile Duct Ligation
steps.instruction: Ligate the common bile duct while preserving blood supply.

substeps.instruction: Gently sweep intestinal contents away from the gallbladder fossa using cotton swabs to expose the common bile duct and pancreas/pancreatic ducts.
Ligate the common bile duct proximal to the pancreatic duct using a 9-0 nylon suture, ensuring no blood supply to the gallbladder or surrounding structures is ligated.

steps.title: Anastomosis Site Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the gallbladder and intestine for connection.

substeps.instruction: Replace the intestines and identify the intestinal segment for the anastomosis.
Make a 1-2mm enterotomy on the antimesenteric surface of the bowel.
Make a ~2mm transverse cut on the gallbladder using surgical microscissors.

steps.title: Create Gallbladder-Intestine Anastomosis
steps.instruction: Suture the gallbladder to the intestine using microsurgical techniques.

substeps.instruction: Juxtapose the gallbladder and bowel; if necessary, use sterile cotton to move the gallbladder and liver caudally for better visualization.
Create the anastomosis moving from the left to right side of the mouse using 9-0 nylon suture and microsurgical needle holders.
Perform the anastomosis in a continuous-running fashion, completing the back row before the front facing portion, with all knots on the outside.

steps.title: Leak Testing and Finalization
steps.instruction: Verify the seal of the anastomosis and close the abdominal cavity.

substeps.instruction: Check for leaks by observing gallbladder distension or by gently pressing on the infundibulum to distend the fundus.
If leaks are detected, seal them using a simple, interrupted 9-0 nylon suture, taking extreme care to avoid tearing delicate gallbladder tissue.
Irrigate the abdominal cavity with warmed, sterile saline.

steps.title: Abdominal Closure
steps.instruction: Close the abdomen using a two-layer interrupted technique.

substeps.instruction: Close the first layer (muscle) using 6-0 polyglactin suture in a simple, interrupted fashion, suturing the connective tissue rather than the muscle proper.
Close the second layer (skin) in a simple, interrupted fashion using 4-0 nylon suture.

steps.title: Immediate Postoperative Care
steps.instruction: Provide immediate recovery support and hydration.

substeps.instruction: Administer 0.5ml of warmed, sterile saline before placing mice in recovery cages.
Keep cages partially on a veterinary-approved heating pad for 5 to 7 days postoperatively.

steps.title: Postoperative Monitoring and Medication
steps.instruction: Monitor animal health and administer scheduled analgesics.

substeps.instruction: Monitor mice for recovery (typically 7-14 days), observing general behavior (bright/alert/responsive vs. depressed/obtunded).
Measure and record weight and food intake weekly.
Administer pain medication: Buprenorphine 0.5 mg/kg every 12 hours for 2 doses (including preoperative dose), and Ketoprofen 5 mg/kg once at 24 hours postoperative.
Provide additional pain medication as needed based on recovery.
